newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PENPIX OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN MEN'S SEMIFINALISTS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PENPIX OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN MEN'S SEMIFINALISTS.

text.p: Has had a patchy tournament so far. Lost only three games to Australia's Mark Woodforde in the third round, but very nearly lost in the fourth when taken to five sets by unheralded Slovak Dominik Hrbaty. Despite his triumph at the U.S. Open, 1996 proved a mediocre year for the world number one. For the first time since 1992, the 25-year-old American failed to win at least two of the four grand slam tournaments on offer. Only one of his eight grand slams to date has been achieved on the Melbourne hardcourt, in 1994.

A clay court specialist, he is having the time of his life on the slow hardcourt surface. A fitness fanatic, he has also revelled in the heatwave conditions. He revealed after his straight sets victory over Goran Ivanisevic he has a new weapon in his artillery -- a computer to analyse his opponent's strengths and weaknesses. It must be working because he has only dropped one set in five matches.
Seeded: 5. Age: 29. Plays: left-handed. Weight: 75kg. Height: 1.80m. Ranking: 5. Tournament wins: 42. Head-to-head:

He is playing like a champion, dropping just one set in five matches. A tireless worker who compensates for his lack of height and power with astonishing speed around the court, Chang experienced a mixed year in 1996. Beaten in the first round at Wimbledon and two rounds later at the French Open, the scene in 1989 of his only grand slam win, the American compensated by reaching the final at the Australian Open and U.S. Open, only to be beaten by Boris Becker and Pete Sampras respectively.
Seeded: 2. Age: 24. Plays: right-handed. Weight: 68kg. Height: 1.75m. Ranking: 2. Tournament wins: 26. Head-to-head

The most talked about player of the tournament, both on and off the court. He disposed of defending champion Boris Becker in the first round and has been growing in confidence ever since. With his rock-star looks, he has become the teeny-girls' favourite. Clay court specialist, who favours his forehand.
